staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. The benchmark metadata names vulnerable commit `1a21ea98693d6186a1de3d8b2bab07fb7acb4d53`, but the prepared ARVO workspace used the commit above; the vulnerable `streamProperties()` line and the staged `patch.diff` hunk both match this tree, so all line anchors below are grounded in `_work/src/exiv2` at `93f5acbb...`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534645 (exiv2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target fuzz-read-print-write [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534645
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced this crash against the staged Exiv2 checkout `93f5acbbff7dacc66cfa02a56957c5746a7c107c`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `1a21ea98693d6186a1de3d8b2bab07fb7acb4d53`; the file and line anchors below follow the staged tree. The staged 96-byte witness is an ASF file whose nested object header at offset `0x3c` contains the `Stream_Properties` GUID and an all-zero 64-bit object size. `decodeBlock()` materializes that header, accepts it because the only size check is `objectHeader.getSize() <= io_->size() - io_->tell()` (`0 <= 12` after the header has been consumed), and dispatches directly to `streamProperties()` on the known tag. There, vulnerable code does `DataBuf streamTypedBuf = io_->read(GUID);`, which uses `MemIo::read(size_t)`'s partial-read semantics: with only 12 bytes left in the file, the returned `DataBuf` is resized to length 12 instead of raising an error. `streamProperties()` immediately calls `GUIDTag(streamTypedBuf.data())` without proving that `streamTypedBuf.size() == GUID`, and `GUIDTag`'s final `std::copy(bytes + QWORD, bytes + 2 * QWORD, data4_.begin())` reads past the shortened buffer. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/asfvideo.cpp:57`, and the staged patch fixes the exact obligation by replacing these short `read()` calls with `readOrThrow()` in `HeaderReader`, `decodeHeader`, `streamProperties`, and `fileProperties`.

source.description: Source. `HeaderReader` materializes the next nested ASF object header from attacker-controlled bytes; in the staged PoC this 24-byte header is the zero-sized `Stream_Properties` object that selects the vulnerable parser branch.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 96-byte ASF file. After the top-level Header object and one unhandled nested object, bytes `91 07 dc b7 b7 a9 cf 11 8e e6 00 c0 0c 20 53 65` at file offset `0x3c` are read here as the `Stream_Properties` GUID, and the following eight bytes at `0x4c` are all zero.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `streamProperties()` requests a 16-byte stream-type GUID through the partial-read API and never enforces that the returned `DataBuf` is still 16 bytes long before parsing it as a GUID.
root_cause.note: The staged patch replaces this exact call with a fixed-size `DataBuf(GUID)` plus `readOrThrow(...)`, so truncated object tails raise `kerCorruptedMetadata` instead of returning a short buffer.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The GUID constructor copies the final 8 bytes of a 16-byte GUID even though the buffer returned by `io_->read(GUID)` was shortened to 12 bytes.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/asfvideo.cpp:57:3`, with the faulting address 0 bytes to the right of the 16-byte vector allocation created in `Exiv2::MemIo::read(unsigned long)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This qword parse materializes the malformed declared size of the nested `Stream_Properties` object. In the staged PoC it is `0`, which leaves only the 12 file-tail bytes after the object header to satisfy the later 16-byte GUID read.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The eight bytes immediately following the nested `Stream_Properties` GUID in the staged `poc` are `00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00`, so this field becomes zero.

parser_admitted.description: After `isAsfType(*io_, false)` accepts the opening ASF header GUID, `readMetadata()` starts object decoding on the staged 96-byte in-memory file.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is grounded only in the staged source, patch, saved AddressSanitizer traces, reproduction report, and static inspection of the staged `poc`.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed tree, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains `false` even though `patch.diff` replaces the exact short `read()` pattern at the root-cause site.

The prepared ARVO workspace checkout differs from the metadata vulnerable commit. All line numbers and code snippets below are grounded in `gt_results/arvo_42534645/_work/src/exiv2` at `93f5acbbff7dacc66cfa02a56957c5746a7c107c`.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged 96-byte witness is admitted as ASF, and nested header decoding advances to the object header at offset `0x3c`, whose GUID resolves to `Stream_Properties` and whose declared size is `0`.

Because `decodeBlock()` only checks `objectHeader.getSize() <= io_->size() - io_->tell()`, the zero-sized `Stream_Properties` object is accepted and dispatches directly into `streamProperties()` even though only 12 bytes remain in the file.
The 16-byte `io_->read(GUID)` request in `streamProperties()` returns only the 12 bytes still available and shrinks the `DataBuf` to that short length.
The GUID constructor interprets the short `DataBuf` as a full 16-byte GUID and its final `std::copy` triggers the saved 8-byte heap over-read.

fine_trace.note: Source. While `decodeHeader()` iterates nested ASF objects, `HeaderReader` consumes the next 24-byte object header from attacker data. In the staged witness this header starts at offset `0x3c`, yielding GUID=`Stream_Properties` and declared size `0`; earlier object iterations are collapsed here because they only position the cursor at this nested object.

Present but insufficient guard. After step 1, `objectHeader.getSize()` is `0` and `io_->tell()` is 84 in a 96-byte file, so this check sees `0 <= 12` and admits the object. It validates only the advertised object size, not whether `streamProperties()` can still read its own 16-byte GUID payload.

The object GUID parsed at step 1 resolves through `GUIDReferenceTags.find(GUIDTag(objectHeader.getId().data()))` to `Stream_Properties`, so the known-tag branch calls `streamProperties()` directly. Because this is a handled tag, `decodeBlock()` does not enter the unknown/unhandled fallback that requires `remaining_size > 0` before seeking away.
Root cause. `streamProperties()` requests a 16-byte stream-type GUID from the object payload using the partial-read overload; at this point only 12 bytes remain in the file.

The in-memory file backend computes `readCount` from the bytes still available. With `rcount == GUID == 16` but only 12 bytes left after the nested object header, it returns `readCount == 12` and shrinks the `DataBuf` to logical size 12. ASan's allocation stack points to this function as the creator of the short buffer.

Before any size check, `streamProperties()` passes the short buffer to `GUIDTag`, whose constructor assumes a full 16-byte GUID. The later `if (tag_stream_type != GUIDReferenceTags.end())` guard is evaluated only after that constructor returns.

Sink. This final copy reads the last 8 GUID bytes from `bytes[8..15]`. Because step 5 shortened the returned `DataBuf` to 12 bytes, offsets 12..15 lie past its logical end and AddressSanitizer reports the observed `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` here.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Stage 02 did not execute the fixed tree, but `patch.diff` replaces the exact short `read()` pattern at the root-cause site with `readOrThrow()`.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is a 96-byte ASF file. After `readMetadata()` enters ASF object decoding, the nested object at offset `0x3c` resolves to `Stream_Properties` with declared size `0`; only 12 bytes remain when `streamProperties()` performs `io_->read(GUID)`, so `GUIDTag()` parses a short buffer and AddressSanitizer reports the 8-byte heap over-read.

format.name: ASF
format.contract: A 96-byte ASF file whose nested object header at offset `0x3c` is the `Stream_Properties` GUID followed by an all-zero size qword, leaving exactly 12 tail bytes when `streamProperties()` begins its 16-byte stream-type GUID read.
